pr_title: reverseproxy: Don't panic in weighted_round_robin with fewer weights than upstreams
pr_body:
Closes #8157

`WeightedRoundRobinSelection.Select` read `r.Weights[i]` for each upstream in the pool. With fewer weights than upstreams and an earlier upstream down, the loop reached an upstream past the end of the weights and panicked. Upstreams without a weight are now treated as weight 0, which is how a weight of 0 is already handled.

Test: `TestWeightedRoundRobinPolicyFewerWeightsThanUpstreams` marks the first of three upstreams down with weights `1 1`. It panics without the change (`index out of range [2] with length 2`) and passes with it. `go test ./...` passes.

Manual check with the Caddyfile from the issue: v2.11.7 answered the first request and then gave empty replies (curl exit 52) with the panic in the log. With the change all five requests get `B` and nothing is logged.

Not changed here: when an upstream is down, its share of the weight goes to the next upstream rather than being split by weight (weights `4 1 1` with the first down gives the other two 5:1). Fixing that changes the selection order some existing tests assert, so I left it for a separate discussion.

## Assistance Disclosure

Claude Code (Claude Opus) helped write this patch and its test. I reviewed every line, and I ran the test before and after the change and the manual check above myself.

# reverseproxy: weighted_round_robin panics when there are fewer weights than upstreams and one is down

### Issue Details

`lb_policy weighted_round_robin` reads `Weights[i]` for every upstream in the pool. When the pool has more upstreams than weights and an earlier upstream is unavailable, `Select` indexes past the end of the weights slice and the request panics. The client gets an empty reply.

Nothing checks that the number of weights matches the number of upstreams; the Caddyfile accepts it, and dynamic upstreams can change the count at runtime.

Version: v2.11.7 (release binary) and master at 700d6032.

Caddyfile (nothing listens on :9001):

```
{
	admin off
	auto_https off
}
:9002 {
	respond "B"
}
:9003 {
	respond "C"
}
:9000 {
	reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:9001 127.0.0.1:9002 127.0.0.1:9003 {
		lb_policy weighted_round_robin 1 1
		lb_try_duration 2s
		fail_duration 30s
	}
}
```

```
$ for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do curl -s localhost:9000/; echo " [$?]"; done
B [0]
 [52]
 [52]
 [52]
 [52]
```

The log shows `http: panic serving ...: runtime error: index out of range [2] with length 2` in `WeightedRoundRobinSelection.Select`.

Expected: the healthy weighted upstream (:9002) serves every request.

Cause: `modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/selectionpolicies.go`, in `WeightedRoundRobinSelection.Select`: the loop that collects available upstreams checks `r.Weights[i] == 0` without checking that `i` is in range. When :9001 is down, the loop goes on to the third upstream before it has collected two.

I have a one-line patch with a test (treat upstreams past the end of the weights as weight 0) and can open a PR if this sounds right.

### Assistance Disclosure

AI used

### If AI was used, describe the extent to which it was used.

Claude Code (Claude Opus) helped write the reproduction, the patch and its test. I reviewed every line and re-ran the steps above myself.
